description:
Anything for dogs around a town, county or point: everything dog-related nearby, grouped by kind: beaches, parks, trails, hotels, campgrounds, cabins, places to eat and rest areas, each sorted by distance, with the dog rule and citation for each. The one call to make when a user names a place and asks "what can I do with my dog there?".

Takes a town or county name (no coordinates needed) or a point. Use dogpolicies_find_hotels when the question is about a specific dog's weight or budget, dogpolicies_plan_trip for a whole stay, dogpolicies_search_places for one kind with filters.

Examples:
  - "What can my dog do in Carmel?" -> place="Carmel"
  - "Dog beaches and parks around South Lake Tahoe" -> place="South Lake Tahoe", types=["beach","park"]
  - "Anything dog-friendly within 5 miles of here" -> near={lat:36.6, lon:-121.9}, radius_miles=5

dogs_allowed_only.description: Leave out places where dogs are not allowed

near.description: A point instead of a town; give one of place or near

per_type.description: Nearest results to show per kind

place.description: A city, county or area in California or Nevada, e.g. "Monterey", "South Lake Tahoe", "Washoe County, NV", "Las Vegas", "East Bay" or "Lake Tahoe"

radius_miles.description: Search radius in miles around the town or point (an area is its own boundary; the radius is ignored)

response_format.description: 'markdown' for readable text, 'json' for structured data

types.description: Kinds to include; all by default

name: dogpolicies_near

citation.description: Copy-ready citation: answer, source, date checked, record URL, license

confidence.description: stated: the place's own source says it; inferred_from_agency: an agency-wide rule; inherited_brand: the chain's policy, not confirmed by this hotel

freshness.description: fresh: inside its review interval; due: past it; stale: past twice it, confirm before you go; unreadable: the last check could not read the source

uid.description: Stable id that survives a rename

title: What is near a town
